notes:
I couldn't write any commentary notes on Isaiah 40, because my research tool stopped working before I could open a single page. On the first attempt it said I had no tool calls left. I tried once more and got the same error. My other tools can't reach the internet.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and fill no gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written verse notes, church-tradition comparisons or other views from memory.

These are the pages I was about to read, if you'd like to check them yourself or ask me to try again later:

- **Verse-by-verse (traditional reading):**
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-40/
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/isaiah/40.htm
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/isaiah/40.htm
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/isaiah/40.htm
  - https://www.preceptaustin.org/isaiah-40-commentary
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/isaiah-40.html (Wesley's Notes)
- **Where traditions may differ:** I planned to search the Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan, Pentecostal and Lutheran sites on your list. I wanted to see how they read v. 3 (the voice in the wilderness and John the Baptist), v. 2 ("double for all her sins") and v. 31 (waiting on the Lord and renewed strength).
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes on netbible.org, Bible Odyssey's articles on the later chapters of Isaiah, and the Catholic and Orthodox sites on these same verses.

If you start a new turn, I'll try the research again and write the notes in the format you asked for.
